method: Second-order polynomial in slope angle alpha with coefficients linear in vw, added to flat-terrain slip; field data
metric: slope-dependent slip regression s(vw,alpha)=(c1*vw+c0)*alpha^2+s(vw) (Eq. 3): c1; c0
unit: unit of alpha NOT stated in the text; implied per (alpha unit)^2; degrees is the only reading giving non-negligible slope effect (see report)
source_title: Data-Driven Terramechanics Approach Towards a Realistic Real-Time Simulator for Lunar Rovers (Kern et al., arXiv 2601.04547v1; iSpaRo 2025)
passage_or_location: PDF p.3, Sec. III.B, Eq. 3; test envelope Sec. III.A p.3: slopes 0 to 18 deg at speeds up to 0.47 m/s
comparability_warning: Alpha unit is undeclared; coefficients are dimensionally inconsistent as printed (dimensionless slip = coefficient x alpha^2 requires hidden units). Under a degrees reading the formula gives slip >1 at 18 deg and 0.47 m/s (computed by the retriever from the printed coefficients), i.e. outside physical range at the edge of the stated test envelope. Even function of alpha, so does not distinguish uphill from downhill although text mentions downward slopes. Rover and sand-specific.
notes: Printed as 's(vw .alpha)' in the PDF text layer. Fit based on averaged values from 16 independent runs. Max speed on slopes (0.47 m/s) is lower than flat max (1.17 m/s) so the vw term is extrapolated for speeds above 0.47 m/s on slopes.
